title: Stop holding the steering wheel like this (Part 1)
hook: Stop holding the wheel at ten-and-two.

script.narration: Stop holding the wheel at ten-and-two. Modern vehicles have steering column airbags that trigger with immense force. If your hands are positioned at the top of the wheel, that airbag can propel your wrists or arms directly into your face.
script.visual_search: driver hands on steering wheel top

script.narration: Instead, keep your hands at nine and three or eight and four. This creates a clear path for the airbag to deploy safely while giving you better control during sharp maneuvers. Follow so you don't miss Part 2!

description: Learn the safest way to hold your steering wheel to avoid injury from airbag deployment. Many drivers still follow outdated advice that puts their wrists in danger. This is part one of our steering safety series.
why_it_will_work: Leverages the success of previous steering wheel content while providing a high-utility safety tip that directly addresses common habits.
